rationale: Registered a successor execution that adds a healing phase to the partition case: after the two sides have each led and committed, the transport connections are restored and the case reports how many leaders remain and whether each side's committed entry is still present. Construction-time local feedback: with the flag enabled the cluster converged to a single leader, yet both divergent committed entries were still present (each on its own side), which the source explains because AppendEntries matches stored entries by index and term only, and the two leaders of the same term wrote different content at the same index, so each side treats the other's entry as a duplicate and never truncates it; with the flag disabled only the one entry ever committed survives.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds a healing phase to the split_configurations case: after both sides have committed, the connections between them are restored, the case waits and then reports the number of leaders and whether each side's committed entry still exists, so convergence and reconciliation after the partition are observed rather than assumed. Comparison set replaced with the convergence and surviving-entry predicates plus the control.

scope.description: What a healed partition leaves behind when one side led on a reconstructed configuration and the other on the committed one. Same twenty-one cases as the predecessor, with the split_configurations case extended: after both sides commit, the transport connections between them are restored in both directions, the case waits twice its election window and then reports the number of leaders on both sides and whether each side's uniquely named committed entry is still present in its log store.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transports; healing uses the transport's own Connect in both directions and no instance is restarted or reconfigured afterwards.
The two sides committed different entries at the same index while both held the same term, as recorded by the split_result event of the same run.
The healed observation window is twice the 800 ms election window, and the entry search uses the same exact payload strings as the pre-heal phase.
The flag-disabled control heals an undivided cluster, so only the entries actually committed there can survive.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, client traffic after healing, membership reconciliation by an operator, and any claim about state-machine contents beyond the presence of the two payloads in the log stores.

experiment.prefix: The extended case is the predecessor's: three peers, both non-leader peers demoted, 100 commands, a snapshot, both peers promoted again, the leader disconnected from them and stopped, only it restarted with a fresh empty instance beside it, both sides allowed to elect and commit uniquely named entries, and a split_result CA_EVENT emitted with both sides' leadership, terms, commit outcomes and cross-entry presence. It now additionally reconnects the restarted side with the two peers in both directions using the transport's Connect, waits twice the election window, counts how many of the three instances are in Leader state, searches the restarted instance's and the two peers' stores for the entry each side committed, and emits a split_healed CA_EVENT with the leader count, whether each side's entry survives, the total surviving entries, the restarted side's state and term, and the healing window in milliseconds.
experiment.responsibility: AppendEntries reconciles a follower's log with the leader's by comparing stored and incoming entries at the same index by term only, so a cluster that reached two leaders in one term depends on that comparison to converge.

comparisons.description: Healing with the flag enabled: after the connections are restored the cluster is expected to converge on a single leader.
Healing with the flag enabled: only one of the two divergent committed entries is expected to remain in the cluster once it has converged.
Control: with the flag disabled only the single committed entry exists, so exactly one survives healing trivially.
